item.title: National Health Insurance: 20 Million Americans, One Expiration Date
item.description:
The U.S. health insurance debate just got a concrete deadline: enhanced ACA subsidies expired, and estimates suggest over 20 million Americans are already feeling the cost. Zara cuts through the political noise to examine what the evidence actually says about national health insurance — the real costs, the real coverage gaps, and what history tells us about mandates, markets, and who actually pays. No party line. Just data.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Topic Frame 02:00 — Segment 1 09:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — The Verdict
Sources cited in this episode: • Mark Shepard, Harvard Kennedy School — analysis of health insurance subsidies debate, October 20, 20 • ACA individual plan premium data — average premiums for a 50-year-old rose 129% since 2014 vs. 68% f • Post-2025 subsidy expiration — enrollment dropped by over 1 million, premiums doubled on average • CBO projections cited by AMA — OBBBA Medicaid expansion end could cause 10 million to lose coverage • Dr. Aizuss, AMA — letter with 90+ physician groups warning about OBBBA Medicaid and ACA premium tax
Next episode: We didn't get to the one question underneath all of this: does MORE coverage actually produce BETTER health outcomes? The data there will genuinely surprise you.

This week, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.4 billion in net inflows over five consecutive days — ending a five-week outflow streak. But here's the catch: Bitcoin barely moved. Marcus sees coordinated institutional accumulation by BlackRock's IBIT near cycle lows. James sees a mechanical illusion driven by AP shorting delays, choppy weekly redemptions, and macro forces that dwarf the ETF story entirely. Someone's right. Someone's wrong. Let's find out.
